function: MIMO symbol detection (DeepSIC equalizer) and soft decoding (unfolded WBP), each module calibrated with modular Bayesian learning for a reliable receiver chain (p. 1, 3-4).
system: Uplink MIMO, K=N=4 single-antenna users and base-station antennas; QPSK/8-PSK (BPSK with polar code (128,64) for decoding); COST 2100 indoor hall 5 GHz; no RIS (p. 9-11).
method: Modular Bayesian deep learning: MC-dropout Bayesian training of each module of deep-unfolded DeepSIC and WBP, sequentially; DeepSIC adapted online from pilots, WBP trained offline, supervised (p. 6-9).
data_channel: Synthetic static linear channel H=e^-|n-k| and non-linear tanh channel; time-varying COST 2100 indoor hall 5 GHz; 128-384 pilots per block, 10 blocks (p. 9-11).
test_conditions: Train on the pilots of each block, test on that block's information symbols; SNR sweep; each channel type trained separately, no unseen scenario (p. 9-11).
baselines: Frequentist and end-to-end Bayesian DeepSIC and WBP, plus a black-box fully connected DNN detector; no non-learned receiver is compared (p. 8-9).
metrics: Symbol error rate, bit error rate and expected calibration error versus SNR (p. 9-13).
complexity: Inference multiplications per Eq. (18)-(20): frequentist Q*K*k(phi), modular Bayesian J*Q*K*k(phi)+Q*K, about J times frequentist; J=5 for DeepSIC, J=3 for WBP (p. 7-9).
q1_support: p. 10: "time-varying COST 2100 geometry-based stochastic channel model" used for Figs. 5 and 10; the other experiments use synthetic linear and tanh channels (p. 9-10).
q2_support: p. 10: "At each block, training is done with 384 pilots, and the SER is computed on 14,976 information symbols"; training is per block and the test is on the same block, with no unseen scenario or stated pretraining.
q3_support: p. 8: "using as benchmarks frequentist learning and standard, non-modular, Bayesian learning"; all compared methods are learned (Figs. 3-10), and no non-learned receiver such as MMSE or BP is shown.
q4_support: p. 7: "the computational complexity in floating point multiplications of applying a DNN"; p. 8: "the inference complexity increases by the ensemble factor", Eqs. (18)-(20).
q5_support: p. 9: "The source code used in our experiments is available at https://github.com/" (footnote 1, repository tomerraviv95/bayesian-learning-in-receivers-for-decoding).
notes: Included, area 1: DeepSIC is the MIMO detector and the WBP decoder is evaluated in cascade, with SER as the main detection metric. q3=0 because every compared method is learned. q2=0 because DeepSIC is retrained on the pilots of each block and tested on that block's information symbols; the paper states no model carried to a new scenario. q1=1 only through the COST 2100 experiments. The text gives 128 pilots for QPSK (p. 9) but the Fig. 3 caption says 384. Title and DOI 10.1109/TVT.2025.3579989 are on page 1; figure legends were checked on pages 10-13.
